p.i: Hostes, Colossos, porticus, & Marmora cum Theatris, stupendos Arcus, sequentum quae fuga temporum, Imbres edaces, atque Aquilo impotens Deiecit & muscus, teguntq; Nunc hedera simul obsoleta, Miratur immortalia si bona Hic esse credant, tempore qui breui Cernent triumphatas opes, & Tot veteris monumenta saecli.

main_text.head: XII. GAL.
main_text.p: LE Babylonien a rengé sous ses loix L'vne des plus grands parts du Monde que tu vois: Le Perse l'a vaincu: luy mesme par apres Ragea son col hautain sous la bride des Grecs[?]: Puis Romme a commandé à la machine ronde, Et Romme ne s'est peu à la fin endurer. Qui es tu maintenant, qui oses esperer, (Les monarques tombez) demeurer ferme au monde?
main_text.head: LAT.

p.i: coegit Gens Babylonia Victrix duello sub iuga maximas. Hanc mox triumphavit pharetra, & Persa gravimetuendus hasta.

page.notes: Top stanza: first line starts mid-verse, continuing from the previous page. Printed "Hostes" and "Theatris" read as shown. The Latin line "Persa gravimetuendus hasta" is printed without a visible space; "gravi metuendus" may be intended. The Latin "triumphauit" is printed with u for v; corrected to "triumphavit". The French rule-marked heading "XII. GAL." is given as level 2 as a numbered part. Roman numeral page number III, running head VANITATE. No catchword or signature visible.
